 🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

Partly is building the AI infrastructure layer for the global automotive parts industry. At the core of that infrastructure is Partly Rails - the transactional backbone that orchestrates the full job lifecycle, from estimation through procurement, reconciliation, and close. It is the layer everything else runs on.

As Principal or Staff PM for Infrastructure APIs & Developer Ecosystem, you own the product that makes Partly's infrastructure accessible to the world. That means owning Rails as an end-to-end transactional product in its own right, building the external API program that lets customers and third-party systems integrate with confidence, and growing the developer ecosystem that compounds Partly's reach across markets without requiring direct Partly involvement in every integration.

This is a platform product role with two connected mandates: keeping the core job flow principled, auditable, and scalable; and building the external developer program - portal, documentation, partner ecosystem, and agentic API evolution - that turns Partly's infrastructure into a platform others build on.

You'll be operating at an inflection point. AI-assisted development and agents are compressing product discovery and delivery cycles. The best PMs we know are no longer waiting for engineering capacity to test an idea - they're building rapid prototypes themselves, deploying them, reading the signal, and deciding within days. We're looking for someone already working that way, or actively building toward it.

💻 What you'll own

 Partly Rails. The end-to-end transactional job flow - from job creation through estimation, procurement, reconciliation, and close. You own this as a product: opinionated in design, reliable at scale, and compelling as a value proposition for any system that runs on it. Key metrics: API feature coverage of the job flow, jobs processed on Rails APIs, uptime, latency, error rates.
 External Integration APIs. The full external API program - API governance, versioning policy, and the standards that define how the outside world connects to Partly. Key metrics: API adoption rate, integration depth, versioning health.
 Developer Portal & Experience. The developer platform - documentation, tooling, sandbox environments, and everything a third-party integrator needs to go from first call to production. Key metrics: time to first test job, time to first production job, developer satisfaction.
 Developer Ecosystem. The global network of integration partners building on Partly's infrastructure - identifying them, activating them, and creating the conditions for the ecosystem to grow. Key metrics: active external integrations, ecosystem growth rate, partner retention.
 Agentic API Evolution. As AI agents become a new class of API consumer alongside traditional system integrations, you own evolving Partly's API offer to serve them - designing for autonomous, context-aware, and reliable agentic usage patterns. Key metrics: agentic integration adoption, reliability under autonomous consumption.



 💻 What you'll do

 Own your product, end-to-end

 Define and evolve the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Partly's infrastructure and developer platform.
 Own the metrics that reflect the health of the Rails transaction layer and the growth of the developer ecosystem - and use them to steer all decisions.
 Lead go-to-market alignment for API releases, ecosystem programs, and integration partnerships.
 Act as the single accountable owner - for successes, failures, and everything in between.



 Stay close to customers

 Maintain direct, regular contact with integration partners and developers - not as an escalation path, but as a core weekly input to prioritisation.
 Understand the difference between what developers ask for and what they actually need to ship successfully.
 Combine qualitative developer feedback with API usage data, integration telemetry, and support signals - and reconcile them.



 Build and ship, not just specify

 Prototype API experiences, documentation flows, and developer tooling yourself using AI-assisted development - fast and disposable.
 Treat the prototype as the hypothesis. Test with real integrators before writing the spec.
 Work hands-on with data: define metrics, build dashboards, query logs, read the signals directly.



 Lead in the human loop

 Partner closely with engineering leads to balance platform capability, developer experience, and technical sustainability.
 Align partner success, GTM, and support teams around the ecosystem strategy.
 Communicate API roadmap and deprecation decisions clearly and early - external developers depend on stability and deserve advance notice.



 Lead in the agent loop

 Design APIs and instrumentation with agentic consumption in mind - not as a future consideration, but as a present design constraint.
 Define what "working" means for agent-consumed APIs: reliability, observability, graceful failure, and context fidelity.
 Think in systems: how does a change to the API surface propagate through every integration downstream?



 Raise the bar

 Set the standard for API design, documentation quality, and developer experience across Partly.
 Help define what an excellent external developer program looks like as the ecosystem scales.



 🥷 What you bring

 Non-negotiables

 Proven experience owning developer-facing API products: API design, versioning, governance, and lifecycle management.
 Practical experience building or scaling a developer ecosystem - partner programs, integration networks, or developer communities.
 Deep understanding of developer experience as a product discipline: what good onboarding, documentation, and tooling actually look like at each stage of maturity.
 Commercial and technical depth - you can engage credibly with engineers on API architecture and translate developer needs into clear business outcomes.
 5+ years owning platform or infrastructure products with clear accountability for adoption metrics, not just delivery.
 You build rapid prototypes yourself - with AI-assisted tools, LLM-assisted development, or code - as a first instinct for testing ideas.
 Strong analytical instinct: you define the metrics, build the view, read the data, and act on it - without waiting for a data team to hand it to you.



 Strong signals we look for

 Experience designing APIs for agentic or LLM-based consumption, beyond traditional system integrations.
 Familiarity with transactional or workflow APIs in domains such as payments, logistics, supply chain, or insurance.
 Experience running a partner or ISV program at scale.
 Comfort owning reliability, observability, and non-functional requirements as first-class product concerns.
 Founder background, or early employee at a platform-first startup that scaled materially.
 You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.



 Bonus

 Domain knowledge in automotive aftermarket, collision repair, or insurance claims.
 Experience scaling developer platforms across multiple geographies.
 Experience with product-led growth motions applied to a developer or API product.
 Experience building or operating products with meaningful agentic or automation components.



 🧭 How you'll think and operate

We're not looking for framework experts or consensus-drivers. We're looking for someone who thinks like this:

 "I shipped a sandbox version of the new flow yesterday. Two integration partners have already tried it. Here's what they got stuck on."
 "The p99 latency spike on job creation is the highest-priority issue this week — not the feature request in the backlog."
 "Here's what the integration telemetry shows. Here's what I think it means. Here's what I'm changing. Here's when I'll know if I'm wrong."
 "An agent just tried to consume this API autonomously and failed in a way we didn't design for. That's the most interesting problem we have right now."



 Speed, ownership, and judgment are the baseline. What differentiates the best candidates is the ability to operate fluently across both the developer-facing surface - documentation, DX, partner programs - and the infrastructure layer beneath it, and to shrink the distance between intent and outcome.

 Please note: if you don't have all the skills or experience listed above but believe you could be outstanding in this role, please still consider applying. Many people count themselves out. We'd love the chance to learn more about you and why you're exceptional.

 Healthy Body, Healthy Mind - We care about performing at our peak. Every team member gets a $1,500 annual wellness allowance (or local equivalent) on a Partly-branded card. Use it on things such as gym memberships, rock climbing, physical therapy, massage, doctor visits, prescriptions—anything that you or your family need!
 Family Comes First - Primary caregivers receive 3 months of fully paid parental leave, plus a flexible return-to-work plan (four days a week at full pay for your first three months back).
 Getting Here Is On Us - If you commute to a Partly office or coworking space, choose from a paid 24/7 parking spot or a commuting allowance. One less thing to think about!
 Workspaces That Inspire - Our brand-new, architecturally designed offices are built for collaboration and creativity, with great coffee, social spaces, and some of the best cafes just a few steps away.
 Office-First with Flexibility - In cities where we have an office (Christchurch, Auckland, London, and Austin), we default to working from the office every day. This lets us move faster, make better decisions, and build strong relationships. We also operate with a high-trust environment, so you can manage your time around your life and flex your schedule to do your best work.
 We Celebrate Together - From weekly happy hours and monthly lunches to quarterly season openers and an annual global offsite, we make time to connect, celebrate, and have fun as one team.

 About Salesforce

 Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

 About The Role

 Technical depth required. Architectural judgment expected.

Salesforce is hiring Senior Forward Deployed Engineers — the Technical Builders, responsible for deciding that leads who design, build, and deploy the most complex agentic AI solutions directly inside enterprise customer environments. You'll lead technical delivery on your team, mentor the next wave of engineers, and set the engineering standards that define how agentic AI gets deployed at scale. Partnering closely with a Deployment Strategist (Strategic Builder - a customer-facing advisor who shapes AI strategy and drives adoption), you'll own outcomes end-to-end, from architecture decision to production. Your passion for well-crafted software that solves real problems will be supported by best-in-class AI tools and a team of talented builders around you.

The Senior Builder Experience

 Technical Ownership: Partner with a Deployment Strategist to own customer outcomes end-to-end. You're the senior technical authority in the room, ensuring deliverables meet the highest engineering standards, whether it was generated by an AI tool by a colleague or written by you directly.
 AI-Supported Engineering: Cursor, Claude, and Salesforce coding products like Vibes are embedded in your daily workflow. The conventions and patterns you develop tend to propagate through the team because other Builders look to your work as reference.
 Roadmap Influence: Your field experience routes directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps you hit and the edge cases you encounter in real life customer environments become the features they ship. Senior Forward Deployed Engineers are the most credible voice in agentic AIproduct evolution.
 Continuous Innovation: You're expected to stay at the forefront — piloting emerging AI tools, experimenting with new models and frameworks, and sharing what you learn with your team and customers.


 What You'll Actually Be Building

 Own end-to-end build and deployment of agentic AI solutions for Salesforce's most strategic customers — from architecture decisions through production handoff.
 Design and ship agentic systems on the Agentforce platform: agent logic, tool calls, multi-agent orchestration, deterministic guardrails, and the integration patterns that hold up in enterprise environments. Your reference implementations become the basis for how other Builders approach similar problems.
 Own the data lifecycle: model design, processing pipelines, and data readiness for AI applications across Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer-specific platforms.
 Resolve the technical blockers that other engineers can't — data integration failures, model deployment issues, orchestration breakdowns, performance regressions. These problems are routed to you because of your track record of solving them.
 Build and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer KPI reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes across engagements.
 Develop proofs-of-concept and MVPs quickly, with the judgment to know which decisions can be deferred and which need to be right the first time.
 Codify what you learn. The patterns, reusable assets, and internal frameworks that come out of your real customer work become the playbooks the rest of the org draws from.
 Mentor other Engineers through code reviews, pair sessions, and shared work. Most of your influence on developing engineers happens inside the same codebases you're building in.
 Provide technical depth on at-risk or strategically critical deployments when senior engineering judgment is needed.

Description

 Join AWS as we invest NZ$7.5 billion in New Zealand over the next 15 years. We're looking for a Technical Account Manager to join our Enterprise Support team and work directly with New Zealand's most ambitious Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) as they build, scale and innovate on AWS.

As a TAM in our ISV segment, you'll be the trusted technical consultant for software companies that are shaping industries across New Zealand and beyond. You'll help ISV customers architect for scale, optimise their cloud operations and accelerate their product roadmaps on AWS. Your day will involve conducting application reviews, leading operational readiness assessments, driving adoption of AWS services that unlock new capabilities and presenting insights at business reviews that influence customer strategy.

This isn't a reactive support role. It's a consulting role where you earn trust through deep technical expertise and deliver measurable impact. You'll work across the full customer lifecycle, from onboarding and migration through to optimisation and innovation, solving complex technical challenges alongside some of the sharpest engineering teams in the country.

You'll be part of a growing Enterprise Support team in New Zealand, backed by the depth of AWS's global technical community. You'll develop your skills across cloud architecture, security, cost optimisation and operational excellence while contributing to Technical Field Communities and earning AWS certifications.

If you want to work at the intersection of cloud technology and software innovation, and you're ready to have a direct impact on how New Zealand's ISVs build and grow, we'd love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities

 Serve as the primary technical advisor to ISV customers, helping them architect, optimise and scale their software products on AWS
 Conduct Operational Reviews, operational readiness assessments and architecture deep-dives tailored to SaaS and multi-tenant workloads
 Drive operational excellence across customer environments by identifying risks, reducing cost and improving reliability before issues impact production
 Lead technical discussions on incident management, trade-offs and risk mitigation, translating complex scenarios into clear recommendations for both engineering teams and senior leadership
 Proactively identify opportunities to accelerate customer outcomes through AWS service adoption, cost optimisation and architectural improvements
 Deliver business reviews that provide actionable insights, track progress against customer goals and strengthen the strategic relationship
 Collaborate with AWS Solutions Architects, Business Developers, Professional Services and Account Managers to deliver coordinated support across the customer lifecycle
 Enable customer teams through targeted workshops, hands-on labs and technical enablement sessions that build lasting cloud capability
 Lead service event reviews and pre-launch planning to ensure customers are prepared for critical launches and operational milestones
 Engage with stakeholders across all levels, from platform engineers to CTOs, earning trust through technical depth and consistent delivery


 A day in the life

No two days are the same, but here's what a typical day might look like.

Your morning starts by reviewing operational dashboards and findings across your customer portfolio, identifying any emerging risks before they become incidents. You notice one customer's database latency has been trending upward and flag it for a deeper review later in the week.

Mid-morning, you lead an Well-Architected Review with a SaaS customer who is preparing to expand into a new market. You work through their multi-tenant architecture, identify areas where they can improve resilience and reduce cost, and leave them with a prioritised set of recommendations they can action immediately.

Over lunch, you join a cross-functional call with the account team to plan an upcoming business review for one of your largest ISV customers. You pull together operational insights, service adoption trends and risk reduction metrics to ensure the review delivers real strategic value.

In the afternoon, you run a hands-on workshop with a customer's engineering team on observability best practices, helping them instrument their platform so they can detect and resolve issues faster. This is the kind of enablement that builds lasting capability and earns trust.

Later, you spend time preparing a pre-launch review for a customer about to release a major product update. You assess their architecture for readiness, review their scaling strategy and ensure their operational runbooks are solid before go-live.

Between meetings, you're contributing to your Technical Field Community, reviewing a SpecReq from a colleague and catching up with your ESM on a customer risk you've been tracking. Every day is a mix of deep technical work, strategic thinking and relationship building.

 About The Team

 Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.

ABOUT US 
 Immersve is a global card-issuing payment institution and principal partner of Mastercard, built to make digital assets spendable in real time on the Mastercard network. We power some of the largest crypto card programs in the world, including Binance, KuCoin, Bitget Wallet and MetaMask; with no bank and no fiat rail involved. We own the full stack, end to end.
 Money is evolving. Its moving onchain faster than most financial systems can keep up with. Stablecoins settle in seconds, run around the clock, and don't care about time zones or banks. Immersve is the last mile: the bridge between web3 infrastructure and the Mastercard acceptance network; turning stablecoin balances into money people can spend today, everywhere Mastercard is accepted.
 Our partners don't have to teach their users a new way to pay. We handle the plumbing so the experience feels exactly like the one people already know. Even works with Apple and Google Pay.
 The next wave of financial institutions won't win by asking customers to change their habits, they'll win by rebuilding what's underneath while everything on the surface stays familiar. That's the problem we're solving at Immersve, and why we're hiring people who want to build it.
 

 Why this role exists 
 Immersve lets crypto and fintech companies issue Mastercard cards backed by on-chain funds. Our partners bring the users and the wallet. We bring the card programme, the issuing and scheme relationships, and the compliance framework behind them.
 Getting a new partner from signed contract to first live transaction is a critical process. It runs across compliance, technical integration and brand work in parallel, and it involves Mastercard, regional issuers, our platform, and the partner's own engineering and compliance teams.
 We are growing the number of partners we onboard each year, and we are building a dedicated team to run it. You are the technical half of that team.
 

 What the job actually is 
 🛠️  Configure our side:  Every partner needs their programme set up in our platform, first in test and then in production. Card products, funding, KYC configuration, fees, credentials, spend controls. You own that configuration and its correctness.
 🤝  Be the partner's technical counterpart:  From the moment integration starts you are the person their engineers talk to. They will ask why a test transaction declined, how the funding flow behaves, what our webhooks do on retry, and why a card did not provision into a mobile wallet. You answer, or you find out and then answer.
 🗝️  Prove it works:  Before a partner goes live they pass a technical certification: a defined set of flows exercised end to end, evidenced and signed off. You run it.
 🔎  Debug across a deep stack:  A single declined authorisation can come from configuration, the card scheme message, a compliance status, an on-chain balance, or the issuer. Working out which, quickly, with a partner watching, is a large part of the job.
 🔦  Own the quiet prerequisites:  The technical groundwork that holds a launch up when it is assumed rather than assigned. You track it and you chase it.
 ⚙️  Automate the repetitive parts. 
 

 The part that makes this different 
 We are an AI-first company and we mean it operationally, not as marketing.
 Much of the setup work above follows a process and is currently manual. We are not hiring someone to do it faster by hand. We want someone who turns it into tooling and agent skills, so that it becomes repeatable and reviewable, and eventually something partners can drive themselves.
 That means you should be comfortable scripting against APIs, working with coding agents as a normal daily tool, and treating your own runbook as something to replace rather than protect. If your instinct on seeing a long manual process is to follow it carefully every time, this is not the right role. If your instinct is to do it once and then write the thing that does it, we should talk.
 

 Your first ninety days 
 Weeks 1 to 4:  Learn the product by using it. Set up test programmes, issue cards, run transactions, break things in the sandbox.
 Weeks 4 to 8:  Shadow a live partner integration. Sit in the channel, answer what you can, escalate what you cannot, and note every question you had to escalate.
 Weeks 8 to 12:  Own an onboarding end to end, and ship the first piece of automation that removes a step you have now done by hand more than twice.
 

 What we're looking for 
 Necessary 
 You have been the technical person facing a customer or partner during an integration, and you are comfortable being the one they message when something is broken;
 You are fluent with REST APIs and webhooks, and with debugging an integration you did not write: logs, request traces, reproducing a failure from someone else's description;
 You can write and maintain scripts. Python, TypeScript, Go, whatever. This is not a software engineering role, but code is a tool you reach for without hesitating;
 You write clearly. Much of your output is written explanation to people who cannot see what you can see;
 You are organised without being told to be. Several partners will be in flight at once, each waiting on something different.

If you've been anywhere near VMware in the last two years you know what Broadcom did to it. Perpetual licences gone, the products you knew folded into VMware Cloud Foundation, pricing moved to per core, and every organisation that built a hosted cloud on VMware now has to work out what their platform costs, what it can do and what they can sell on top of it. Collada has been engaged by a large New Zealand telecommunications provider to find a Product Architect to answer exactly that for their hybrid cloud offering.
 The platform is being upgraded to VCF 9. That work sits with the platform team and the architecture is well in hand, what they don't have is someone who can take the capability that upgrade unlocks and turn it into product. Service tiers, the catalogue, self-service, what gets metered and how it's priced, and the proposition sales can take to market. The role sits between the people building the platform and the people deciding what to sell, and reports to the head of enterprise platforms and architecture, who is an architect himself and will want someone who can hold their own on both sides of that line.
 That's the filter. You need to be credible in an architecture review board talking about multi-tenancy, NSX, vSAN and how the service catalogue should behave, and equally credible in a product strategy session arguing about packaging and margin. In my experience most people are strong on one side and bluff the other. If your VMware experience is operating or migrating platforms and you've never had to think about what a customer pays for, this probably isn't it. If you've been a vendor or partner architect, built or productised a hosted VMware service, or sat on the service provider side through the Broadcom transition, it very likely is.
 There is also a customer-facing edge to it. A good chunk of this provider's customers are on VMware themselves and facing the same Broadcom decisions, so the propositions this person defines will be used to bring those customers onto the new platform.  Opportunity to work on modern software engineering and AI-related initiatives.

 Direct involvement with technical teams and business stakeholders.

 Higher Level Security Clearance

About the Role
 Traffic Safe NZ is a 100% New Zealand owned and operated company that provides temporary traffic management services throughout the North Island.
 We are seeking an experienced Software and Applied AI Engineer to build, enhance and support enterprise software, internal AI tools and practical agentic systems.
 This hands-on individual contributor role combines full-stack development, legacy application support, AWS cloud-native engineering and AI-assisted delivery. You will independently own work from requirements through production support, collaborate with IT Operations and business stakeholders, and contribute to architecture and engineering standards.
 Key Responsibilities
 Own end-to-end software delivery: Analyse requirements; design, develop, test, deploy and maintain secure, scalable applications with performance and resilience appropriate to business-critical workloads.

 Maintain and modernise existing systems: Fix defects, develop features and integrations, and incrementally improve legacy applications while new systems are developed.

 Coordinate application support: Work with IT Operations and support colleagues to triage requests, agree priorities, investigate production issues, perform root-cause analysis, coordinate fixes and releases, and maintain support documentation.

 Build full-stack solutions: Develop backend services, REST APIs, integrations and web applications using C#, .NET, JavaScript/TypeScript, Angular, SQL and NoSQL. Design databases and optimise queries.

 Manage releases and cloud delivery: Maintain builds, environment configurations, deployment automation and CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, AWS CodeBuild/CodePipeline, Jenkins or similar platforms. Support AWS containerised and serverless applications and environment automation.

 Ensure quality, security and reliability: Write maintainable, documented code and automated unit, integration and functional tests. Contribute to code reviews, architecture and engineering standards. Implement DevSecOps checks, authentication, authorisation, least-privilege access and secure secrets handling. Monitor availability, logging and performance; address recurring faults and improve backup, recovery and resilience.

 Build AI engineering tools and business workflows: Develop tools supporting requirements, design, code generation, testing, documentation and delivery. Build and support LLM integrations, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agentic systems that plan tasks, use tools and APIs, execute workflows and verify results.

 Direct and validate AI-assisted work: Use Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, Cursor or comparable tools, remaining accountable for generated work. Define agent tasks, context and acceptance criteria; conduct separate reviews and obtain human sign-off at agreed decision points.

 Make AI solutions reusable and controlled: Create shared skills, prompts, agents and workflow components. Evaluate accuracy, reliability, latency and cost; implement logging, access restrictions, safeguards and fallback or human review paths. Protect confidential data and credentials, restrict agent actions and mitigate malicious instructions in retrieved content or tool responses.

 Collaborate and improve: Work with business stakeholders, engineering teams and external vendors; share knowledge and improve development workflows, automation, testing and engineering practices.

 Required Skills and Experience
 Mandatory: 6+ years of full-time enterprise software development and production support experience . Internships may not count towards this minimum.

 Experience with C# and .NET Framework and/or modern .NET, such as .NET 8 or later. Experience in other stacks, including Java, Node.js or Python, will also be considered.

 Frontend development with JavaScript/TypeScript and Angular; sound knowledge of REST APIs, backend services, distributed applications, object-oriented programming, SOLID principles and design patterns.

 Hands-on SQL and NoSQL experience, such as Microsoft SQL Server and MongoDB, including complex queries, stored procedures and database performance optimisation.

 Experience with Git, collaborative development, enterprise builds and releases, CI/CD, automated deployments, and unit, integration and functional testing using modern frameworks.

 Experience maintaining legacy applications, triaging defects, troubleshooting production issues and performing root-cause analysis. Ability to coordinate with IT Operations and support teams and clearly communicate progress and resolutions.

 Hands-on AWS application development, deployment and support across relevant compute, storage, database, networking, security and monitoring services. Relevant services include EC2, Lambda, S3, RDS, API Gateway, Elastic Load Balancing, IAM, Secrets Manager and CloudWatch. Depth in services used in delivered applications matters more than coverage of every service listed.

 Familiarity with Docker, containerised architectures, microservices, scaling, deployment and image management using ECS, Fargate and ECR. Kubernetes familiarity is also relevant.

 Ability to automate engineering and operational tasks using Python, Bash or PowerShell.

 Understanding of secure coding, authentication, authorisation, application security and DevSecOps, including dependency scanning, secret scanning and CI/CD security checks.

 Regular use of coding assistants or development agents, with evidence of reviewing generated changes for behaviour, security and test coverage.

 Practical experience building AI applications, internal development tools or agentic workflows using LLM APIs connected to business data, application services and tools.

 Understanding of prompt and context engineering: clear instructions, suitable examples, relevant project knowledge and controlled tool access.

 Familiarity with harness and loop engineering: configuring agent execution environments and using tests, feedback, iteration limits and completion criteria to guide work.

 A traceable approach to AI-supported delivery, with separate implementation and review, agreed governance and human sign-off for significant decisions.

 Awareness of AI risks, including confidentiality breaches, exposed credentials, prompt injection, excessive permissions and unreliable responses. Examples of documented, reusable prompts, skills, agent configurations or automation shared with colleagues.

 Clear communication, practical problem-solving and attention to detail, with the ability to work independently across teams, explain technical issues to business users, prioritise deliverables and follow issues through to resolution.

 Desirable Skills
 React, Next.js and Node.js.

 Microservices and event-driven systems using SQS, SNS, EventBridge or Step Functions.

 Infrastructure as code using Terraform, AWS CDK or CloudFormation, and delivery automation using GitHub Actions or AWS developer tools.

 AWS data integration and processing, including Glue; backup, disaster recovery and high availability.

 Observability using CloudWatch, X-Ray, OpenTelemetry or similar tools.

 Amazon Bedrock or other managed AI platforms; orchestration frameworks, RAG, embeddings, vector search and automated AI evaluation.

 Delivery through multiple AI agents, including task decomposition, coordination, validation and integration of outputs.

 Agile/Scrum delivery and support of business-critical production systems and internal enterprise platforms.

 Qualifications and Personal Attributes
 A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology or a related discipline is preferred.
 You will be practical, reliable, organised, delivery-focused and calm under pressure, with strong analytical thinking, ownership, follow-through and documentation habits. You should be comfortable balancing legacy support with new software and AI delivery, maintaining confidentiality, sharing knowledge and proactively improving processes. Curiosity about emerging AI capabilities and sound judgement about when human review is needed are essential.
 Working Rights
 Applicants must already hold valid New Zealand work rights. Visa sponsorship is not available.
 How to Apply
 Submit your CV and a brief cover letter explaining your interest in the role and how your experience meets its requirements.

The rockets and satellites we build and launch enable some of the most ambitious and vital space missions globally, supporting scientific exploration, Earth observation and missions to combat climate change, national security, and exciting new technology demonstrations. Neutron will be our next rocket on the launch pad, an advanced 13-tonne payload class, reusable rocket to launch the mega constellations of the future. Our space systems business includes our extensive line of satellites and components that have enabled more than 1,700 missions including the James Webb Space Telescope, NASA Psyche Mission, Artemis I, Mars Ingenuity helicopter, and more.

Configuration Management Engineers combine technical and process excellence with strengths in technical planning and communication. This position is ideal for a multidisciplinary engineer keen to support a complex project from design realisation through to integration and launch.

• 1+ Years relevant work experience

• Proven track record of collaborating with cross functional stakeholders to guide projects from concept to completion
• Proven communication skills and the ability to build strong working relationships with colleagues and engineering professionals
• The ability to work to tight deadlines within a high-pressure environment
• Strong desire to learn new material in order to solve difficult, ambiguous challenges

• Project Management experience
• Working knowledge of SQL Databases
• ERP Experience

At RUSH, we design, build, and manage purposeful digital experiences that improve people’s lives. 

 


 You'll build the security into the systems we design, build and run for clients, in code and infrastructure as code. You'll start on a large greenfield platform on Microsoft Azure for a major New Zealand client, embedded in its delivery team from design through to production.

 This is a senior engineering role with a lot of autonomy: you'll own security design and implementation on your engagements. You'll write authentication and authorisation flows, harden cloud infrastructure, wire security into CI/CD pipelines and build the audit trails and telemetry that let us detect and investigate. Developers and platform engineers moving into security are welcome.

 


 What you'll build 

 


 Identity and access 

 
 Build sign-in and federation using Microsoft Entra ID B2C and OpenID Connect integration with client identity platforms (Entra External ID).

 Implement MFA flows (e.g. AuthSignal) and SCIM provisioning.

 Build role-based and field-level permission models in code, so access is enforced consistently across every part of the system.

 Build session and token handling: HTTP-only cookies, HTTPS-only transport, idle timeout and server-side revocation.

 
 


 Application security 

 
 Implement input validation and output encoding against SQL injection, XSS and the rest of the OWASP Top 10, on client and server.

 Implement malware scanning on every file upload path.

 Secure API authentication, authorisation and integration points with external systems.

 Manage secrets and certificates through Azure Key Vault, removing them from code and config.

 
 


 Cloud hardening, as code 

 
 Configure Azure WAF (Application Gateway), Azure Front Door and DDoS protection through infrastructure as code (Bicep or Terraform).

 Set secure baselines with Microsoft Defender for Cloud, and fix what Wiz finds across development, staging, UAT and production.

 Build privileged access controls: bastion hosts, VPN, segregation of duties and privileged device baselines.

 Protect non-production environments to production standards, or build the anonymisation pipeline that makes production data safe to use.

 
 


 Pipeline security 

 
 Integrate SAST and DAST into Azure DevOps pipelines, scanning every build and failing on high-severity findings.

 Tune the tooling so findings are actionable, and help developers fix them.

 
 


 Audit logging and detection 

 
 Build audit trails that record who changed what, when, and the before and after state.

 Ship infrastructure and application logs to long-term retention, with export.

 Instrument the system and write detections (KQL in Azure Monitor) so attacks are visible.

 Investigate, contain and fix incidents at code and infrastructure level, and keep the incident runbook tested for fast P1 response.

 
 


 Security leadership in delivery 

 
 Own security design decisions on your engagements, approving security-relevant architecture before it's built.

 Lead threat modelling at design and sprint planning, using OWASP and NIST SSDF.

 Write security stories and acceptance criteria into the backlog, so security ships in every sprint.

 Review security-sensitive code, pair with developers on fixes, and lift the delivery team's security capability.

 Act as the security technical lead for client engineering teams.

 
 


 Working with the GRC and security operations team 

 We're a small team, so you'll sometimes help out beyond engineering. It isn't the core of the role, but expect to work with the GRC and security operations team on:

 
 compliance evidence for the controls you build (ISO 27001, SOC 2, tracked in Vanta)

 technical answers for client security questionnaires and audits

 scoping penetration tests and fixing their findings

 monitoring, incident response exercises and incident response for systems you've built

 
 


 You'll need 

 
 5+ years in software, platform or security engineering, including at least 2 focused on security, shipping production code in a team.

 A track record of owning security design and implementation.

 Strong coding in at least one mainstream language (e.g. C#, TypeScript, Python).

 Infrastructure as code (Bicep or Terraform) on Microsoft Azure.

 Deep hands-on Azure: networking, Entra ID, Key Vault, WAF, Front Door and Defender for Cloud.

 A strong understanding of OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, SCIM, RBAC and MFA flows.

 Knowledge of the OWASP Top 10 and how to prevent each class in code.

 CI/CD experience, ideally Azure DevOps, and scripting in PowerShell or Python.

 
 


 Nice to have 

 
 KQL and Azure Monitor or Log Analytics.

 Wiz or another cloud security posture tool (Prisma Cloud, Orca).

 SAST and DAST tooling (SonarQube, Checkmarx, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP).

 NIST SSDF, and experience fixing penetration test findings.

 Exposure to ISO 27001 or SOC 2.

 Certifications such as AZ-500, SC-200 or OSWE, or a bug bounty, CVE or CTF track record.

 Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora is the country's largest employer, delivering universal public healthcare to 5 million New Zealanders.

 We provide essential hospital, specialist, and community health services across 80+ locations — from large urban centres to rural towns and remote communities.

 As a Research Project Manager, you will play a critical role in supporting the successful delivery of the Lung Screening Mobile Pilot, leading the research workstream that will generate evidence to inform the future implementation of a national lung screening programme.

 In this role, you will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and monitoring the research activities associated with the pilot programme. You will work closely with clinicians, researchers, implementation teams, and technical experts to develop and manage key research components, including study protocols, participant materials, ethics and locality approvals, data management processes, privacy documentation, and research governance requirements.

 The ability to manage multiple workstreams and competing priorities while maintaining a strong focus on delivery and quality

Good at solving the problems that don’t come with an instruction manual? 
 o   Variety without being stuck in one lane. Machinery, packhouses, process plant, fault-finding, upgrades and commissioning.
 o   Help build something. Join JWE as we grow our automation capability across the Bay of Plenty, with genuine opportunity to grow with it.
 o   Just straight talk, good banter, no politics, Just good humans doing quality work and backing each other to win
 If you’re technically capable, love figuring out how things work and want more variety, ownership and opportunity than your current role gives you, this might be your next move
 

 WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU — AND WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT 
 Let’s be honest.
 A lot of companies throw around words like culture , development , and teamwork … but behind the scenes it’s the same work, the same problems, limited opportunity, and engineers stuck in their own lane.
 That’s not us.
 At JWE, we’re building something properly.
 We’re a well-established industrial electrical and automation business with strong relationships across the Bay of Plenty. We work across packhouses, packing machinery, production lines and industrial processing plant where quality, reliability, problem-solving and getting the job done properly actually matter.
 We’re now looking for an exceptional Automation Engineer to help build the next stage of our automation capability.
 This isn’t a “sit behind a desk and write PLC code all day” automation role.
 This is a hands-on technical role for someone who thrives on:
 o   solving complex plant and machinery problems,
 o   understanding how processes actually work,
 o   PLC and HMI programming,
 o   fault-finding and troubleshooting,
 o   improving and modernising existing systems,
 o   commissioning solutions and seeing them work in the real world,
 o   and constantly learning and improving their technical capability.
 You’ll sit right amongst the action, connecting automation, machinery, process, electrical, operators and real-world problem-solving.
 And as JWE continues to grow, you’ll have the opportunity to help shape how our automation capability develops across the Bay of Plenty.
 If you’ve built real technical capability and want more variety, more ownership and a bigger runway for where your career could go, you’ll fit here.
 If you enjoy that combination, keep reading.
 

 YOUR MISSION (SHOULD YOU CHOOSE TO ACCEPT IT…) 
 To understand how plant and machinery should work, solve the problems when they don’t, and develop smart, reliable automation solutions that make our customers’ operations better.
 You’ll work closely with our electricians, technicians, customers and wider team to take automation challenges from problem through to solution — whether that means fault-finding an existing machine, modifying a PLC programme, improving a process, upgrading legacy equipment or commissioning something new.
 Your responsibilities will include:
 o   Developing, modifying and fault-finding PLC and HMI systems, predominantly Omron
 o   Systematically diagnosing plant, machinery and process faults
 o   Understanding how the whole machine or process works — not just the code
 o   Developing practical automation solutions that are reliable, maintainable and fit for purpose
 o   Commissioning new systems, modifications and upgrades on site
 o   Working with motors, VSDs, sensors, instrumentation and industrial control equipment
 o   Troubleshooting and improving existing and legacy control systems
 o   Working alongside our electrical team to solve complex plant problems
 o   Supporting breakdowns, shutdowns and commissioning when required
 o   Taking ownership of problems and seeing solutions through properly
 o   Looking for opportunities to improve plant reliability, performance and automation
 You’ll also play a key role in helping build and shape JWE’s automation capability across the Bay of Plenty as we grow.
 

 THE TYPE OF WORK WE DO 
 Our teams work across a wide range of industrial environments throughout the Bay of Plenty, including:
 o   Packhouses & packing machinery
 o   Production lines & conveyors
 o   PLC & HMI automation systems
 o   Industrial manufacturing & processing plants
 o   Machine control & sequencing
 o   Motor control & VSD systems
 o   Instrumentation & process control
 o   Coolstores & industrial refrigeration
 o   Existing and legacy control system upgrades
 o   Plant breakdowns & technical fault-finding
 o   Machinery modifications & automation improvements
 o   Industrial shutdowns & commissioning
 Some jobs start with a blank sheet.
 Others start with “this machine has stopped and nobody can work out why.”
 Both are part of the job.
 No two weeks look the same — and that’s exactly how we like it.
 

 OK, ON TO YOU... 
 We're open to talking to Intermediate through to Senior Automation Engineers.
 We're more interested in what you can actually do than collecting qualifications.
 You might come from automation, mechatronics, mechanical engineering, process engineering, industrial electrical or another hands-on technical background.
 What matters is that you can understand how things work.
 You'll ideally bring: 
 o   Solid industrial automation experience
 o   PLC programming and fault-finding capability
 o   Experience with HMI systems
 o   Omron experience would be highly desirable, but isn't essential if you're strong on other PLC platforms
 o   Good understanding of machinery, industrial processes and control systems
 o   The ability to systematically diagnose faults rather than simply changing things until something works
 o   An understanding of motors, VSDs, sensors, instrumentation and industrial control equipment
 o   The ability to understand existing systems , including equipment that's been operating longer than some of us have
 o   Strong problem-solving skills
 o   Good communication skills and the confidence to work alongside operators, electricians and customers
 o   The ability to work independently while still being part of a team
 o   A willingness to get out on site and get amongst the plant
 o   A full NZ driver's licence
 Experience in packhouses, food processing, manufacturing, refrigeration, production machinery or other process-driven industries would be a big advantage.
 

 THE PERSON WE'RE REALLY LOOKING FOR 
 We're looking for a problem solver.
 Someone who doesn't panic when the answer isn't obvious.
 You gather the information.
 Understand the process.
 Work through the problem logically.
 Find the cause.
 Develop the solution.
 Test it properly.
 And leave the plant better than you found it.
 You take ownership of your work, communicate when something isn't going to plan and ask for help before a small problem becomes a big one.
 High standards. Low ego.
 

 WHERE COULD THIS GO? 
 This is where things get interesting.
 We're not recruiting an Automation Engineer simply to fill a vacancy.
 We're building our automation capability in the Bay of Plenty.
 As JWE grows, we want to build a stronger automation team around the industrial customers we already support.
 For someone with the capability and ambition, that creates a genuine opportunity to grow with us. You don't need to want management to work here — a great technical engineer can build a great career with us too.
 But if you do want more, there is room to grow.
   
 PURPOSE 
 Delivering excellence — seamlessly. 
 JWE exists to make people’s lives better because they’ve been connected to us.

As a Senior PM, you'll lead execution-intensive projects that require deep research, prototyping and sustained coordination.
 Beyond project leadership, you'll own the operational cadence of a pod made up of engineering, product and design, running grooming sessions, and retros that keep engineering and design aligned and moving. You'll report into the Head of Product and work alongside the rest of the product team, collaborating closely with the Head of Design and engineering leads on a daily basis.

The people we have in mind may have started in product, design, research, or engineering, but they now use AI and code to move faster from question to answer: from a user problem to a working prototype, from raw data to a clear insight, from a one-off fix to a process the team runs every cycle.

 Lead projects end to end by taking ownership of execution-intensive projects from discovery through to delivery. Define the problem, conduct research, build prototypes, work with a designer and data analyst, and ship the outcome.

 Generate project proposals - identify opportunities from research topics, capability improvements, and technical opportunities, and shape them into well-defined project proposals.

 Own product ceremonies for the pod by running coarse and fine grooming sessions with design and engineering, and lead cycle retrospectives.

 Manage project execution - create tasks, assign them to triage, groom them with engineers, and own all project communications including status updates, stakeholder alignment, and rollout comms. This also includes acting as a bridge between product and marketing where relevant.

 Immerse in the tooling and become well versed in using Linear, managing project setup, workflows, and label configuration as well as maintaining the backlog. Field product-related questions via Slack and email, keeping the team unblocked.

 You’re fully comfortable working with data on your own, and you treat it as a core input to every product choice. You understand user behaviour, design and read experiments, and measure outcomes, so your decisions rest on evidence rather than instinct.

 Build AI product literacy by understanding how our AI system behaves, where they fail and how they’re evaluated. Use that to frame problems, design experiments and set quality bars for AI-powered features.

 You build what you imagine. AI and code are increasingly part of your practice. You use tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or whatever comes next to prototype and ship rather than stopping at the handoff. You don’t need to be a traditional software engineer, but you should be technically capable and comfortable working inside a codebase.

 You think in systems. You don’t just want to make the artifact. You want to understand the thinking behind it and turn that thinking into a workflow, tool, agent behavior, or reusable capability.

 You have high agency. You are comfortable with ambiguity, move quickly from exploration to output, and don’t need a playbook before you start.

 Strong research skills — you can design a research approach, lead interviews, and synthesise findings into actionable recommendations.

 Deep data fluency - you can take a fuzzy question, work out what data answers it, and turn the analysis into clear insight that drives product decisions.

 The ability to take ambiguous problems and structure them into clear projects with well-defined tasks and milestones.

 A collaborative working style — you'll be working alongside a designer, engineers, and other PMs as peers on a daily basis.

 You’re driven to find the right problems to solve and the best ways to solve them. You also care about how product processes work, and you’re always looking for ways to improve them.

 5+ years of product management experience

 Experience running product ceremonies in a cross-functional team

 Strong proficiency with project management tools (Linear, Jira, or similar)

 Experience with user research — planning, conducting, and synthesising qualitative research

 Comfort interpreting product data — dashboards, experiment results, and behavioural analytics

 Strong data fluency with knowledge of SQL and/or Python for ad-hoc data exploration

 Strong cross-functional delivery: planning, sequencing, stakeholder comms

 Nice to Have:

 Familiarity with AI/ML product development and experiment evaluation

 Experience working in a small, fast-moving team where you wear multiple hats

 Experience presenting complex concepts to audiences

About Halter 
 At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
 We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, BOND, DCVC, Blackbird, Promus Ventures, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures.
 To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram.
 About the role 
 We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. We can’t wait a decade to find out whether a design will survive - so we have to know before it ships. That’s the job of our Reliability team.
 As a Reliability Engineer, you’ll be the person who turns “it needs to last” into evidence. You’ll own reliability for products and subsystems through development: assessing risk early, designing accelerated tests grounded in physics of failure, building the models that link hours in a chamber to years on a cow, and making a clear, evidence-backed call on whether a design is ready. You’ll close the loop with the field, comparing what fails out there with what our testing predicted, and changing our tests where they missed.
 What you’ll do 
 Own the reliability plan for a product or major subsystem through development - turning reliability goals into measurable requirements, test plans and acceptance criteria

 Lead risk assessments, including failure mode and effects analysis and fault tree analysis, and review designs for robustness alongside mechanical, electrical and firmware engineers

 Design and run accelerated tests, including highly accelerated life testing and accelerated life testing, built from first principles and physics of failure, with clear learning goals and decision criteria

 Build reliability and acceleration models that link test time to field life, and write scripts and tools to automate repeated data analysis

 Correlate field failures with test results - show where our testing caught a failure mode, flag where it didn’t, and develop new test methods to replicate the field stresses we’re missing

 Write reliability reports and sign-off recommendations that others can audit, with residual risk and the evidence behind it made clear

 Assess the reliability impact of design, component, production and supplier changes, and work with suppliers on component qualification

 Improve our lab capability - evaluating and introducing new test equipment, fixtures and methods, and scoping and reviewing work from external labs

 Mentor and support junior engineers, reviewing their test setups and data and explaining the reasoning behind our methods

 This is a hands-on, first-principles role. We're looking for someone with real experience in reliability or hardware test engineering who wants to go deep on the craft - and who will hold the line on an unwelcome conclusion when the evidence supports it. We’re open on level and will work out the right fit through the interview process, from an experienced individual contributor through to someone ready to set technical direction for the team.
 What you’ll bring 
 Several years of experience in reliability, test or hardware engineering on electronic or electromechanical products - a degree in electrical, mechanical, mechatronics or materials engineering, or similar, is preferred

 Hands-on experience designing and running reliability tests, such as accelerated life testing, highly accelerated life testing, or environmental and mechanical stress testing

 A solid understanding of how electronic products fail - for example solder joint fatigue, corrosion, moisture ingress, battery degradation and connector wear - and the physics that drives them

 Confidence with reliability statistics and modelling, such as life data analysis, acceleration models, confidence levels and sample sizing

 A first-principles mindset - you want to understand why a test represents the field, not just that it follows a standard

 Clear, honest communication grounded in evidence. You can explain risk and uncertainty to people outside your discipline, and you’ll hold your ground on an unwelcome conclusion when the data backs it

 Strong sense of ownership and a bias for action - you see what needs doing and get on with it without waiting to be asked

 A tenacious curiosity to figure things out, and the process discipline to do it properly every time

 Low ego, highly collaborative and willing to play for the front of the Jersey.

 Join our team 
 Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!
 If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!
 Please also feel free to check out the careers page for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn & Instagram.
 Why our team loves working at Halter: 
 Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.
 Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

 You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our personal growth fund.

 This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

About APLYiD 
 APLYiD is an AML compliance platform for small and medium businesses across legal, real estate and accounting. We are moving from a legacy checks product to a full workflow platform, and expanding acrossNew Zealand, Australia and the UK.
 About the Team 
 Core + Integrations is one of our two product portfolios. Core is our legacy checks product, roughly £8m of revenue, and the strategy there is to protect and maintain it. Integrations is the new unit within it, and it sits at the heart of our go-to-market globally: every new market and every partner we bring on depends on it.
 There is no established playbook here yet. Whoever takes this on is building the operating model this function runs on for years to come, not inheriting one.
 About the Role 
 Integrations need to be in place ahead of our UK hard launch, and we are hiring for this now rather than waiting until the roadmap is overflowing and delivery starts slipping. This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Product, with no direct reports.
 You will own the integrations roadmap and backlog, work directly with the engineering squad on partner builds, and coordinate directly with partners through the build and go-live motion.
 This role sits alongside our Global Partnerships Initiative, you are involved before a partnership is signed, not only after. The Global Partnerships Manager owns the commercial relationship, the deal itself. You bring the technical and product view into that evaluation, data structures, integration cost, delivery risk, so a partnership that looks right commercially doesn't turn out to be a poor technical bet once it's already signed. Once a deal is done, you own the product relationship: what we build, what needs to change, and the ongoing relationship with the partner's technical and delivery teams.
 You also own Core. That is a protect-and-maintain remit, not an active build one: when something breaks orneeds fixing, you are the owner who triages it and gets it resolved. The active building energy in this rolegoes into Integrations; Core is about keeping what already exists running well.
 What You'll Do 
 Assess and own delivery of integrations with CRMs, practice management systems, ERPs, and verification providers such as our biometrics and credit bureau partners, working from partner API documentation to scope what we build.

 Own the integrations roadmap and backlog, including how new global partnerships get planned into it, so priorities across markets, Australia and the UK, for instance, get weighed deliberately rather than fought over.

 Keep existing integrations and partners, running as we scale: partner-side fixes and changes, and customer-side support when something breaks, not just new builds.

 Build and hone the relationship with each partner's product and technical teams, distinct from the commercial relationship the Global Partnerships Manager owns.

 Support go-to-market motions for integrations, working with marketing, sales and customer success so partner integrations translate into signed and adopted customers.

 Manage stakeholders on both sides: internally across engineering, marketing and sales, and externally with partner teams.

 Partner with the technical engineering lead on integrations to set product strategy and direction, not just delivery.

 Own Core on a protect-and-maintain basis: triage issues as they surface and get them fixed, rather than driving new build work there.

 What We're Looking For 
 Real experience with complex system integrations: you can look at an API and a data model and work out how one system should talk to another, and you can hold your own in that conversation with engineering.Alongside that, genuine product management capability, because this role carries the same accountability for roadmap, backlog and delivery as any other product role here.
 Fluency in AI, and an interest in using it to scale how this function runs, is important. For example, we would like API documentation drafted automatically from requirements rather than written up by hand. Familiarity with Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a real advantage, since it gives our integrations layer a shared way of understanding how different systems can talk to ours. You do not need this on day one, but you do need a point of view on it and a willingness to build that fluency fast.
 What Success Looks Like 
 The first 90 days are not about redesigning the function, they are about building and implementing the operating framework for how integrations work, both internally and externally. You will do this along side our Global Partnerships Manager, and it needs to connect four layers: technical, commercial, product, and marketing and communications. Get that framework in place and you have done the job we hired you for.

 Troubleshoot device and firmware issues directly on Linux/Ubuntu environments

 Integrate test automation into our CI/CD pipelines so quality checks run with every build
